content.title: How Bayern Munich beat Real Madrid in pulsating Champions League tie to tee up semi-final against PSG
content.text: The two European giants traded seven goals and a red card as Vincent Kompany’s men won 6-4 on aggregateBayern Munich will face Paris-Saint Germain the semi-final. Getty ImagesBayern Munich 4-3 Real Madrid (6-4 agg.) — resultBayern Munich are heading for the Champions League semi-finals after beating Real Madrid 6-4 on aggregate.An 86th-minute red card for substitute Eduardo Camavinga preceded two late Bayern goals to eliminate the record winners.Luis Diaz and Michael Olise got the goals in the closing stages to set up a semi-final between Vincent Kompany’s men and Paris Saint-Germain. Until the red card, it had been a much-improved Madrid performance as they scored three times in the first half, twice through Arda Guler and once through Kylian Mbappe. But they were beaten and it likely means they will go without a trophy for the second season in a row.Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementGet briefed on Bayern Munich 4-3 Real MadridDid you miss that bonkers first half?Or wonder how the tactical battle unfolded?Well, look no further than The Briefing where our writers tuck into all the biggest topics. You'll find a fresh take on that match on the link below.What next for Bayern? Getty ImagesBayern return to Bundesliga action on Sunday at home against Stuttgart.They will be back in the Champions League with their semi-final against PSG on April 28.What next for Real Madrid? Getty ImagesThe odds of Arbeloa's side ending the season with a trophy are looking pretty slim as focus returns to La Liga and trying to catch Barcelona. Madrid are next in action at home against Alaves on Tuesday.Arbeloa: ‘Not at all worried about my future’ Getty ImagesTime will tell if this ends up being a consequential evening for Alvaro Arbeloa and his future as Real Madrid manager.Here’s what he said on that topic after the match:💬 “I’m not at all worried about my future. Since I’ve been in this position, it hasn’t been the slightest concern. I feel I’ve done everything I could to try and help my players win every day.“Right now, I’m not thinking about any of that at all. I’ll say it again: it’s the club’s decision and I’m a loyal supporter; all I want is for Real Madrid to win, regardless of who’s in charge.”Kane on his 50-goal season: 'I’ll do what it takes to help the team' Getty ImagesIn his post-match chat with TNT Sports, Harry Kane was reminded that he is the first English player to score 50 goals in a season for a team in Europe’s major leagues since 1931. Here is what he had to say about it.💬 “It’s a reward for a lot of the hard work we put in. Not just me, but the team. It wouldn’t be possible without the players around me. For me it’s just about keeping it going.“We’ve still got weeks six weeks left in a Bayern shirt, we have a World Cup in the summer and I want to stay physically fit, sharp and be out there to help the team. I’ll do what it takes to help the team: scoring goals, defending, assists, whatever it is.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementData digest... explaining how Bayern won that game The pass networks of both teams show their stylistic differences. Bayern attempted to pass Madrid into submission (69% vs 31% possession) while Madrid were content sitting deep and hitting on the counter (12 fast breaks vs 4 for Bayern).Arbeloa's side even created more xG than Bayern (2.3 to 2.1) but Kompany's team pulled away in the end after Camavinga's red card.Match dashboard: Bayern Munich 4-3 Real Madrid 33 shots, 14 on target, 7 goals - how good was that?!The very best of European footballGenuinely, that was among the very best games I've ever seen live. Full of tension and drama, quality and — in the end — plenty of acrimony. That is what the very top of European football is supposed to look like.Man of the match: Michael Olise The mercurial Bayern forward takes home the official man of the match trophy tonight and who can argue with that!A stunning winning goal and a stellar performance on the biggest stage.Let's hear from Alvaro Arbeloa Getty ImagesThe Real Madrid manager has been speaking to TNT Sports. Here’s how he reflected on that match:💬 “That was a great match. We put players like Miliato, Bellingham out there who could not play in the first leg. We had a great match here, we scored three goals and we had the chances to score more goals. Witht the red card everything was over. “It’s unbelievable that you send off a player for this action. I can;' believe that. It’s not possible to be sent off for an action like this. We feel really angry and disappointed and all of this is hard for us. “In La Liga everything is difficult, we are nine points difference from Barcelona. We have matches to play and we need to be at our best.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMadrid players skip media No Madrid player has spoken to Movistar TV after the final whistle. They are so angry that they're boycotting the flash zone, reporter Sergio Sanchez has just said on the Spanish channel.Bayern's Kompany gamble paying off Nancy mentioned the journey that Michael Olise has been on from playing for Reading in the Championship to downing Real Madrid on the European stage. But how about Bayern manager Vincent Kompany, who two years ago was overseeing Burnley’s dismal Premier League campaign? That season ended in the club getting relegated back to the Championship, with Kompany then moving to Bayern.The German giants took a big risk in hiring the former defender, but clearly it’s paid off. They’re flying high in the Bundesliga and into the Champions League semi-finals. Photo of the night That's what it means for the Bayern fans, who were in fine voice all night.One of the most impressive Kop ends in European football.Kane: It feels amazing Getty ImagesHarry Kane scored his 50th goal of the season this evening and he spoke to TNT Sports after the victory.💬 “It feels amazing now, for sure. It was a tough game, we knew it was going to be difficult. Real Madrid in the Champions League have a special connection and you need to be at the highest level to beat them — and knock them out.“First half was a little bit crazy and we got off to the worst start possible, but we got back into the game well and looked like the team who was more dangerous. We were a little more patient in the second half and we knew we’d get stronger as the game went on, and we were able to take our chances towards the end.”Arsenal through without too much trouble Getty ImagesArsenal are through to the Champions League semi-finals after a game that lacked cutting edge, quality and even, in the end, much in the way of psychodrama.Mikel Arteta’s side did not play especially well. They were, however, able to hold Sporting at arm’s length for much of the evening, which made it a more comfortable experience than many were fearing.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCold from Olise The celebration that sealed Bayern's place in the semi-final!Olise has been on some journey from Reading in the Championship to beating Real Madrid in the Champions League. Progress.Harry Kane enjoyed that one Who can blame him!Bayern's star man on the score sheet again tonight — his 50th goal of the season!A reminder of the goals as they went in Getty ImagesIf you're having trouble remembering the order of tonight's seven goals, well, who can blame you? Here's a recap:1' Guler (Bayern Munich 0-1 Real Madrid)6' Pavlovic (Bayern Munich 1-1 Real Madrid)29' Guler (Bayern Munich 1-2 Real Madrid)38' Kane (Bayern Munich 2-2 Real Madrid)42' Mbappe (Bayern Munich 2-3 Real Madrid) 83' Diaz (Bayern Munich 3-3 Real Madrid) 90+4' Olise (Bayern Munich 4-3 Real Madrid) A good omen for Bayern? Getty ImagesYou have to go back six years for the last time neither Real Madrid or Barcelona made it to the Champions League semi-finals.That campaign finished in empty stadiums and the team that lifted the trophy was … Bayern Munich.The team they beat in the final? Paris Saint-Germain.
